transcript.author: late_night_ops
transcript.body: Ask HN: Our worker queue silently loses about 3% of jobs at peak. Redis lists with BRPOP, workers in Python, nothing in the logs. Where would you look first?

transcript.author: cache_person
transcript.body: Have you checked the maxmemory policy? If it is allkeys-lru the list itself can get evicted.

relation.evidence: no own messages in the thread

reference.text: BRPOP removes the job from the list before your worker has done anything with it. A worker that crashes or gets killed between the pop and the end of processing loses that job with nothing in any log, and peak is exactly when workers get OOM-killed. Two things to check before touching Redis config: count pops versus completions per worker for an hour (the gap is your 3%), and look at worker restarts in that window. If that is it, move the job to a per-worker processing list on pop (BLMOVE) and reap stale ones; that is the reliable queue pattern and it costs one extra command.
reference.rationale: A new entry into somebody else's thread: it has to add something the thread does not have. The one existing reply covers eviction; the account's actual experience is the pop-then-crash loss and how to measure it. One concrete mechanism, one measurement, one fix.

later_messages.author: late_night_ops
later_messages.body: It was the pop-then-crash thing. Workers were getting OOM-killed at peak. Thanks all.
